ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, and a tangent line extending to the right is drawn at a point below the circle; from the same point there is also a chord/secant slanting up to the left, intersecting the circle again at the upper left. The minor arc between the two intersection points is marked as 100° in the figure, and angle 2 is located between the rightward ray of the tangent and the chord slanting up to the left; it is the larger angle. Then reason: angle 2 is the angle formed by the tangent and the chord, and it intercepts the major arc opposite the 100° minor arc. The measure of the major arc is 360° - 100° = 260°. According to the tangent-chord theorem, the angle formed by a tangent and a chord equals half of its intercepted arc, so m∠2 = 260° / 2 = 130°.
